q: The Radon–Nikodym theorem states that if ν ≪ μ (ν is absolutely continuous w.r.t. μ), then:
opts: There exists a measurable function f ≥ 0 such that ν(A) = ∫_A f dμ for all measurable A
μ and ν are mutually singular
exp: The Radon–Nikodym derivative (density) f = dν/dμ exists precisely when ν ≪ μ. This generalises the relationship between a probability density and a measure.
